purpose: Teach: ウニ/髭/洋書/つば/にんにく/マヨネーズ/ヤギ/泡盛

lines.speaker: hiroshi_elder
lines.jp: ばあさん、若い頃、お父さんが北海道でウニを召し上がったぞ
lines.en: You know, Gran, when your father was young, he ate sea urchin up in Hokkaido.
lines.style: Soft, nostalgic opening. Gentle reach into memory. Measured pace, almost reverent. Like he's handling something precious that's been tucked away for decades.

lines.speaker: sachiko_grandma
lines.jp: うん、お祖父ちゃん、晩年は白い髭を蓄えてらしたわよね、あなた?
lines.en: Yes, and your grandfather—he had such a beautiful white beard by the end, didn't he, dear?
lines.style: Warm and conversational, gently steering. She's not correcting him so much as offering her own memory alongside his. Slight upward lilt on the question, inviting connection.

lines.speaker: hiroshi_elder
lines.jp: ばあさん、若い頃、お父さんが書斎に洋書を並べてらしたぞ
lines.en: Gran, when your father was young, he used to line his study shelves with Western books.
lines.style: Same patient, nostalgic tone as before. Slightly more deliberate this time—he's settling into the rhythm of remembering. Quiet reverence for the detail.

lines.speaker: sachiko_grandma
lines.jp: お祖父ちゃん、お孫様にお茶を飲ます時、つばが飛ばないようにご注意なさってたわよね、あなた?
lines.en: Your grandfather was always so careful when he poured tea for the grandchildren—made sure nothing would splash, you remember that, don't you, dear?
lines.style: Tender and specific. She's naming a small kindness with the weight it deserves. Warm, knowing tone—like she's drawing him into shared memory. Slight pause before 'dear,' giving the thought room to land.

lines.speaker: hiroshi_elder
lines.jp: ばあさん、若い頃、お父さんがにんにく料理を好まれたぞ
lines.en: Gran, when your father was young, he was quite fond of garlic dishes.
lines.style: Continues the gentle, reverent pace. The memory is simpler this time, but delivered with the same care and weight. Quiet admiration underneath.

lines.speaker: sachiko_grandma
lines.jp: お祖父ちゃん、お弁当にマヨネーズを少し付けて下さったわよね、あなた?
lines.en: Your grandfather always put just a little mayonnaise in our lunch boxes—such a small thing, but he never forgot, did he, dear?
lines.style: Warm, almost tender-amused. She's spotlighting a small act of care with genuine affection. The detail matters to her. Soft, intimate tone—like she's sharing something only she would know.

lines.speaker: hiroshi_elder
lines.jp: ばあさん、若い頃、田舎でヤギを飼っていらしたお家にお邪魔したぞ
lines.en: Gran, when your father was young, we once visited a house out in the countryside where they kept goats.
lines.style: Slight shift—a touch more animated, like he's seeing the scene again. Still wistful, but with a small thread of liveliness. The memory has texture now.

lines.speaker: sachiko_grandma
lines.jp: お祖父ちゃん、沖縄旅行で泡盛を飲まれたわよね、あなた?
lines.en: Your grandfather drank awamori on that Okinawa trip, didn't he, dear? I can still picture him.
lines.style: Warm, intimate, close. She's bringing the memory into sharp focus—almost seeing him there. Slight smile underneath the words. The 'dear' carries both affection and a gentle anchoring back to the present.
